issues.description: The problem UML specifies an Animal constructor with signature Animal(String, int) (including an age parameter), but the provided solution and the usage in the template Main use single-argument constructors (e.g. Seal("Clarabelle")). This mismatch in constructor parameters will confuse students about which constructor to implement and which signatures tests expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent across artifacts. Either update the problem statement/UML to require Animal(String name) (matching the template Main and solution), or change the template and solution to provide and use Animal(String, int) and update example usages accordingly.

issues.description: The UML and problem text list an 'age: int' attribute for Animal, but the solution's Animal class has only a 'name' attribute (no age). This attribute mismatch between the specification and the solution/template can confuse students about required fields, getters/setters, and constructor responsibilities.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the specification and implementation: either remove the age attribute from the UML/problem statement if age is not intended to be part of the exercise, or add the age field (with getter/setter) and update constructors in the template and solution to include and initialize age.
